summary: In this excerpt from Book 3, the narrator, distraught after a phone call with Steve about their future and possible parenthood, looks at herbal extracts given to her by Ramala and wonders whether to take them. She recalls the warning from Hannah Klein about Alex Goddard, then calls Hannah on a Sunday after reaching an answering service, reporting that she passed out at an infertility clinic the previous day. Hannah listens without reprimand but is unimpressed by the Goddard connection, and the narrator asks her to brunch to review the herbs.
one_line: A distraught narrator calls Dr. Hannah Klein about herbal extracts from Alex Goddard after fainting at an infertility clinic.
key_facts: The narrator tells Steve that she may have to go to a sperm bank if she cannot count on him.
Steve says he misses the narrator and needs time to think about their next step.
The narrator recalls Megan, an engineer living in Witbank, as another source of mixed signals.
Ramala gave the narrator bottles of "herbal extracts" on the way out, and she is unsure what they are or what they have to do with "centering".
The narrator reminds herself never to take something when she does not know what it is.
The narrator calls Hannah Klein's number on a Sunday and reaches an answering service with a southern-sounding voice.
The narrator tells the answering service, "No, this is an emergency."
The narrator tells Hannah she was at an infertility clinic yesterday and passed out.
Hannah had specifically warned the narrator not to go near Alex Goddard.
Hannah says little about Alex Goddard and does not sound impressed.
The narrator asks Hannah to brunch so she can show her the herbs Alex Goddard gave her and get her opinion.
Hannah says she was just headed out to Zabar's.
